name: Verified-active creator lists for indie Steam launches
buyer: Solo or tiny-team indie developer with a demo or launch, no marketing budget and no creator contacts
pain: Finding creators who are real and active, then emailing keys and tracking results. One comparison page estimates 10-40 hours per 100 keys. Some creator lists are stale.
wedge: Sell per-launch lists of creators verified as active, filtered by genre and recent upload date, at a one-time $15-69. The entrant cannot replicate Keymailer's network. The wedge is data freshness only, and gameoutreach.co already occupies the one-time-pack position.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: One-time pack priced at the top of the $15-69 range, using public data APIs whose costs are small (owner estimate). It is built and sold by a solo founder with no creator network.
scan1Edge.falsifier: gameoutreach.co already sells packs from $15, so if its packs have the same freshness and no developers pay for the entrant's lists, there is no edge.

substitutesNoted.name: gameoutreach.co
substitutesNoted.price_point: One-time packs from $15 after a free preview

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: Model: midpoint of the $15-69 one-time range, with ~80% gross margin per the owner's estimate because data-API costs are small. Developers launch seasonally and few will pay more than ~$70 per game.

majorUncertainty: Whether developers will pay for verified-active lists when a $15 direct competitor exists and Keymailer has a free tier.
unknowns: Whether Keymailer annual pricing is $149 or $249 (sources conflict)
Whether the 2-5 hours per 100 keys estimate is achievable
Whether the data APIs allow this use under their terms
Actual conversion of developers to paying customers
gameoutreach.co's actual list quality and volume
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on YouTube/Twitch data access and terms of service. Contact scraping carries CAN-SPAM exposure and Steam key handling carries fraud risk.

evidence.publisher: Keymailer Alternatives in 2026: Where Indie Devs Send Steam Keys Now
evidence.shows: Manual key outreach is estimated at 10-40 hours of developer time per 100 keys (a vendor blog estimate, not primary user data).
evidence.quote: Somewhere between 10 and 40 hours of your time per 100 keys, once you count research, writing, follow-ups, and bookkeeping.

evidence.shows: Keymailer has a free plan capped at 10 network campaign requests a month, paid plans from $24.99/mo and promoted boosts from $249.
evidence.quote: Free plan capped at 10 network campaign requests a month; paid plans from $24.99/mo; promoted boosts from $249.

evidence.shows: An itch.io developer reports creator accounts whose last stream was 8 years ago, which points to stale lists.
evidence.quote: There were accounts that had their last streaming 8 years ago.

evidence.shows: A developer applied for Keymailer membership and got no response for a week, so the incumbent is slow to onboard.
evidence.quote:
https://interestick.itch.io/cs

I applied for Keymailer membership, but it has been a week and I haven’t received any response.

evidence.shows: gameoutreach.co already sells a free preview, then one-time packs from $15 with no subscription, so the one-time-pack wedge is taken.
evidence.quote: Free preview first, one-time packs from $15, no subscription.

evidence.publisher: Keymailer Alternatives in 2026: Where Indie Devs Send Steam Keys Now
evidence.shows: Woovit no longer distributes keys, so a former competitor has exited.
evidence.quote: Publisher records were archived and remain retrievable by email, but the platform no longer distributes keys.

evidence.shows: A community manager says it is hard to find teams that have budgeted for marketing at all, which limits willingness to pay.
evidence.quote: In my experience as a Community Manager, it's difficult to find teams that have budgeted for marketing at all.
